title: AI Voice & TTS News Briefing
summary: Covers Wed Nov 18, 7:52 AM to Thu Nov 19, 7:52 AM MT. Two new developments, both dated Nov 17 and not covered in earlier briefings. HeyGen released Avatar 6, which generates presenter video in a person's own voice from a photo and can re-voice single edited words while leaving the rest of a recording untouched. ElevenLabs added a beta API that checks audio for its watermark, cut speech-to-text prices for self-serve and Business plans, and added pronunciation-rule highlighting in Studio. The watermark check arrives two weeks before the EU's Dec 2 deadline for marking AI-generated audio.

articles.title: HeyGen Avatar 6: presenter video in the person's own voice, with word-level edits that leave the rest of the take untouched (missed earlier)
articles.summary: HeyGen released Avatar 6, an avatar model that builds a talking presenter from one photo (optionally plus a short recording), at up to 2K with no fixed length, and voices it with HeyGen Voice in the person's own voice. Gestures follow the script or written motion cues, two speakers can share one frame, and an editor can replace individual words in a recorded video, regenerating only that span in the speaker's voice. It is available in the web app, mobile app and API, with consent checks for realistic video references. HeyGen says raters judged it 84.4% indistinguishable from real footage in side-by-side tests, by its own evaluation. Why it matters: correcting a line in finished presenter video without a reshoot could cut revision cycles in localized training and message video. Independent arena tests covered only short English-centric clips, so long-form, multilingual lip-sync quality and consent policy should be checked before use.

articles.title: ElevenLabs adds a watermark-check API, cuts speech-to-text prices and highlights pronunciation rules in Studio
articles.summary: ElevenLabs' Nov 17 release notes add a beta content-provenance endpoint that checks an uploaded audio file for an ElevenLabs watermark and, where possible, returns the product, model, generation time and a generation ID (never the prompt or account). Speech-to-text now costs $0.20 per hour for batch and $0.22 per hour for real-time on every Scribe model for self-serve and Business plans; Enterprise pricing is unchanged. Studio audiobook projects now highlight words matched by pronunciation rules and explain conflicts when several rules match. Why it matters: a way to verify whether audio came from ElevenLabs supports provenance checks and disclosure records ahead of the EU's Dec 2 marking deadline, and the pronunciation highlights make lexicon review easier for language reviewers. The watermark check is beta, ElevenLabs-only, and detection reliability after editing or re-encoding is not documented.
